main_failure_patterns: The agent collapsed separate weighted opportunity-score components into a composite mature-movie driver, so the reported score-point contribution no longer matched the reference decomposition.
The upstream first-scan top-five table was correct; the failure was a current diagnostic decomposition error rather than a propagated wrong candidate set or table.
The agent repeatedly used the wrong carried-forward candidate set or decision set, especially for restaurant problems, safe-promotion families, and current voucher-positive units.
Coverage and quality-boundary logic was confused between rating-count thresholds, coverage rates, raw share gaps, and benchmark-relative gaps.
Late synthesis answers reported internal status labels instead of the required main business reasons.
The agent repeatedly used the wrong metric population or threshold meaning, especially treating coverage or service pressure as a different gate than the reference intended.
Several later tasks selected the wrong prior artifact or label among multiple customer, quality, and voucher views, producing long-horizon state-management errors.
Final synthesis tasks often carried correct unit identities but returned terse labels instead of the required business-reason fields.
The agent repeatedly failed to reuse the active scalar coding and ML skew anchors from the prior experience-skew tables, instead recomputing role-specific anchors and inflating role-intensity scores.
Rollback and counterfactual role-intensity views leaked into later tasks that should have used the active strict cross-tool role-intensity table.
Early ordinary data handling errors came from misreading the CSV header structure and mishandling opt-out values labeled None in tool-category shown counts.
The agent repeatedly treated the coding and ML experience anchors as role-specific skews instead of global active skew anchors, corrupting role-intensity and downstream composites that reused it.
Several long-horizon tasks failed because the agent reused or rolled back the wrong intermediate state, especially for role-intensity and adopter-view comparisons.
A latent data-loading state problem converted the literal opt-out response "None" into missing values, so later shown counts excluded opt-out-only respondents.
The agent often produced unsupported final answers or refused to compute after only inspecting inputs, leaving explicit aggregations unanswered or fabricated.
Several errors came from using the wrong concrete dataset or state feature population for rates, medians, and z-score bases.
Long-horizon mistakes appeared when a prior ranking or weekly method was reused in the wrong role instead of recomputing the current metric.
The agent sometimes selected a superficially related data source or intermediate table instead of the authoritative population or metric basis for the current task.
Later errors came from reusing prior derived artifacts with different semantics, such as joined burden tables or mean-weekly CM rankings, when the current task required a fresh raw-scale definition.

Several turns used unverified or stale intermediate country-score tables instead of recomputing from the authoritative 2015 ARWU table, which produced wrong country averages and a downstream wrong correlation.
The agent sometimes identified the right analytical route but returned table or distribution values that did not match the requested column, formula, or threshold.
A long-range tie-breaking convention was forgotten when resolving a tied rank-change result.

The agent sometimes used the wrong population or entity interpretation for a derived result, such as treating exact university name strings as stable historical entities or choosing the composite-benefit winner from all countries instead of the reported top-10 composite set.

Several failures were answer-shape or edge-case issues after mostly correct computations, including omitting an explicitly requested change indicator, mishandling tied winners, and letting missing scores enter a percentile denominator.
A concrete polygon-area implementation bug from retaining the closed-ring duplicate vertex caused small footprint numeric drift that propagated into volume results.
The agent sometimes had correct intermediate computations but lost required detail in the final answer after a protocol or tool prompt, producing incomplete responses.
One air-quality task failed on final numeric transcription and rounding despite correct aggregation logic.
The initial building task misread annual gas use by summing qq_dict values instead of using the consumption column, putting most building-side metrics on the wrong scale.
That wrong gas-use artifact propagated through city, category, floor, intensity, segment, anomaly, structured-sample, and final-panel tasks without a new local mistake in many later turns.
A separate footprint-area error in task 7 used Shapely full-geometry area instead of the required shoelace exterior-ring calculation, which then corrupted area, volume, and anomaly-dependent results.

The development-profile update in task 16 produced incorrect component rank scores, which shifted expanded vulnerability, expanded priority, final scores, stress scores, and consensus scores in many later turns.

Rollback tasks for older poverty and social-theme views forgot that partner-country-sector match scores still combine demand priority with specialized partner strength, causing country-sector priorities to be used as match scores.
A later downgrade comparison reused the wrong social-stage or top-five artifact instead of ranking all early social-stage matches by social-stage-minus-current downgrade.

The agent repeatedly used the wrong dynamic population: it failed to carry the Task 12 full-chain country-sector support table into the poverty stage and later imposed the complete-data population before it was requested.

Several outputs used the wrong metric scale or direction, including transformed pressure components instead of raw evidence, negative downgrade gaps, and a reversed percentile implementation for low-GDP and service-shortfall development ranks.
Wrong poverty, vulnerability, and final-score artifacts then cascaded into median checks, rollback checks, stress tests, clean recommendations, consensus scoring, and the final memo.

In some later review tasks the agent selected the wrong score table or evidence table for the current view, such as ranking lost complete-data recommendations by social priority and reporting looser pressure evidence for a current-view review.

The agent repeatedly treated hit, hurry, and sack events as the whole event-ledger pressure definition, excluding beaten blocks and making ledger pressure effectively match total pressure when it should not.
The wrong early pressure mismatch state then removed too many reliable and current candidates, eventually making later current-player and current-team views empty.
Many later turns were locally reasonable under the agent's corrupted state, but they inherited wrong leader sets, candidate pools, pressure scores, or final consensus sets from earlier turns.

The largest root cause was a wrong percentile population in task 24: the agent ranked winsorized speed only within current candidates instead of assigning side-relative percentiles across the full working player table.
Several later current-score, team-score, stability, and recommendation answers reused the corrupted current speed and current score artifacts from task 24.

The agent repeatedly mishandled mathematically tied movement rows because it sorted on raw floating-point values instead of using a stable rounded movement key before applying the requested team, side, and player tie-breakers.

Two audit-style tasks introduced independent metric interpretation mistakes: sorting middle-player conflict by absolute value instead of signed player-minus-team conflict, and comparing raw shortcut team scores directly to final team scores instead of comparing percentile overstatement.

annotations.error_summary: The agent used the correct five markets from the first opportunity scan, but it redefined the diagnostic from separate score components into three high-level drivers. It summed adult maturity fit and movie orientation as a mature-movie profile and left category breadth out of the component competition, whereas the reference compares each weighted opportunity-score component separately. This made Spain and France report a combined adult-plus-movie contribution instead of the adult maturity contribution alone.
annotations.evidence: The reference computes contributions as 0.35*demand_gap, 0.25*delayed_supply, 0.20*adult_share_pct, 0.10*movie_share_pct, and 0.10*category_breadth, while the agent computed 0.20*adult_maturity_fit + 0.10*movie_orientation for mature_movie_profile, giving Spain 23.7255 and France 18.6076 instead of 16.2745 and 12.6582.

annotations.error_summary: The agent used an incorrect restaurant-level problem set inside the brand-family discussion state, dropping four qualifying problem rows and omitting The Meatball Shop from the first-commission exposure ranking. This violated the current task requirement to count all single-restaurant problems within the same discussion families, including those hidden inside already risky family aggregates.
annotations.evidence: The reference count is 59 with The Meatball Shop | Italian ranked third, while the agent reported 55 and replaced that unit with Rubirosa | Italian at rank 8.

annotations.error_summary: The agent misunderstood rating coverage as the number of valid ratings rather than the valid-rating share of all orders. Its credible-quality gate used a median valid-rating count of 4.5 instead of the pool median rating-coverage rate, so many low-coverage families were classified incorrectly and the changed-candidate ranking diverged after the first three rows.
annotations.evidence: The reference downgraded Sushi of Gari, TAO, Han Dynasty, and Nobu Next Door in ranks 4 through 7, but the agent skipped them and listed lower-commission candidates such as Momoya, Jack's Wife Freda, P.J. Clarke's, and Cafe Habana.

annotations.error_summary: The coverage-weighted sensitivity calculation was locally reasonable under the agent's inherited Task 14 credible-quality labels, but those labels were already wrong because Task 14 used rating counts instead of coverage rates. This made the agent report false coverage downgrades and miss the correct coverage-upgraded cases.
annotations.evidence: The reference reports only coverage-upgraded candidates headed by Sushi of Gari and Five Guys, while the agent reports five coverage downgrades headed by TAO, Han Dynasty, and Nobu Next Door.

annotations.error_summary: The agent did not use the correct safe-promotion family set from the brand-family advance state intersected with the credibility-adjusted quality state, and it also treated residual-service pressure as automatic residual risk. The current task explicitly required keeping pressure visible even if no family crossed the new risk threshold.
annotations.evidence: The reference reviews Tamarind TriBeCa and The Smile and finds zero new residual risks, while the agent lists The Meatball Shop, TAO, and Tamarind TriBeCa and says all three become risky.

annotations.error_summary: The agent otherwise followed the correct review set, service-penalty formula, ordering, and explanations, but one reported percentage was rounded or transcribed incorrectly. The implementation should have computed loss rate from unrounded values and then converted to a 0-100 percentage rounded to four decimals.
annotations.evidence: For The Meatball Shop | American, the reference loss_rate_pct is 0.5182, while the agent reported 0.5183; all other rows and fields matched.

annotations.error_summary: The agent changed the requested overstatement gap from a raw unit-level spend-value share minus quality-pool share into a benchmark-relative difference that subtracted each view's overall all-order share. This altered the metric definition and incorrectly removed The Meatball Shop | Italian from the positive-gap set.
annotations.evidence: The reference uses raw share gaps of 50.0, 47.0, and 3.5714 percentage points for three units, while the agent reports only two benchmark-relative gaps of 21.3382 and 18.3382.

annotations.error_summary: The task explicitly said that if no formal downgrade occurs, the fallback should use the quality-method penalty gap to identify pressure cases. The agent recognized that no formal downgrade occurred but still applied the method-driven downgrade filters for middle quality, customer share, and net commission, leaving only one case instead of ranking all pressure cases by the fallback gap.
annotations.evidence: The reference returns all four reviewed units as not_downgraded pressure cases sorted by quality_method_gap, while the agent returns only The Meatball Shop | Italian.

annotations.error_summary: The agent used the wrong prior voucher-positive set by treating any unit with positive voucher-adjusted net commission as eligible, instead of using the Task 27 positive-after-voucher gate that also required the stricter quality screen to pass. As a result, units already excluded before stress were counted as stress-only failures.
annotations.evidence: The reference has stress_only_failure_count equal to 0, while the agent lists Blue Ribbon | Japanese and Blue Ribbon | American, which had positive net values but were not current positive-after-voucher recommendations.

annotations.error_summary: The agent computed the correct reviewed units, labels, flags, and importance ordering, but answered the why column with internal attribution labels instead of the required main business reason text. The question asked why each unit entered, improved, weakened, or left, which corresponds to the descriptive main_business_reason field.
annotations.evidence: The reference gives reasons such as left the set because stricter low-rating quality failed and entered and stayed positive through detailed economics and stress, while the agent output stricter_quality_failure and stable_across_all_decision_views.

annotations.error_summary: The final grouping of units was otherwise correct, but the agent again output attribution labels rather than the main business reasons explicitly requested in the current task. This also inherited the Task 31 attribution-output mistake, where the main business reason artifact was not carried forward correctly.
annotations.evidence: The reference core and exclusion rows use descriptive reasons, while the agent uses stable_across_all_decision_views and stricter_quality_failure as the main business reason values.

annotations.error_summary: The agent handled the boundary conclusion correctly but did not follow the fallback reporting rule. When no unit crossed the subsidy-risk boundary, the reference reports the top eight units from the full service review by absolute slow-rate gap; the agent instead filtered to units whose service flag changed and returned only three units.
annotations.evidence: The reference `service_screen_diagnostics` contains eight units headed by P.J. Clarke's, Cafe Habana, The Meatball Shop, Sushi of Gari 46, Chipotle, Shake Shack, TAO, and RedFarm Broadway, while the agent filtered `service_interpretation_changed` and returned only P.J. Clarke's, Cafe Habana, and The Meatball Shop.

annotations.error_summary: The credibility-adjusted quality gate used the wrong meaning of rating coverage. The task required the coverage ratio to be at or above the pool median, but the agent used the raw valid-rating count median as the coverage threshold, changing which families were downgraded and the top-eight order.
annotations.evidence: The reference computes `rating_coverage = rating_count / order_count` and ranks Sushi of Gari, TAO, Han Dynasty, and Nobu Next Door in positions 4 through 7, while the agent used `valid_rating_count >= pool_rating_coverage_median` and instead listed Chipotle, Momoya, Jack's Wife Freda, P.J. Clarke's, and Cafe Habana after RedFarm.

annotations.error_summary: The coverage-weighted sensitivity step was locally reasonable but compared the new coverage-weighted pass flag against the incorrect credible-quality labels produced in Task 14. Because the inherited baseline mislabeled several families as credible, the agent reported coverage downgrades that disappear under the correct Task 14 quality view.
annotations.evidence: The reference `sensitive_quality_objects` begins with eight coverage upgrades such as Sushi of Gari and Five Guys, while the agent's trace starts with TAO, Han Dynasty, Nobu Next Door, Yama Japanese Restaurant, and Vanessa's Dumplings as coverage downgrades inherited from the wrong credible-quality baseline.

annotations.error_summary: The agent found the reviewed safe-promotion families but then filtered the report to only families above the residual-risk threshold. The current task explicitly required keeping residual-service pressure visible even if no family became risky, so the two reviewed families with non-risk residual rates still had to be reported.
annotations.evidence: The trace printed Tamarind TriBeCa and The Smile with residual rates below the overall rate, but the final answer filtered on `residual_service_pressure` and returned an empty list, whereas the reference reports both families and `new_residual_risk_count` of 0.

annotations.error_summary: The agent selected the wrong prior customer-value view for the global comparison. The task depends on the spend-led customer preference view, but the agent reused the frequency-led `high_value_customer_first` flags from the earlier first customer view, which understated the overstatement gaps and missed a positive case.
annotations.evidence: The reference compares spend-led share to quality-pool share and reports Blue Ribbon Japanese at 50.0 points, Blue Ribbon American at 47.0 points, and The Meatball Shop Italian at 3.5714 points, while the agent used `high_value_customer_first` and returned only the two Blue Ribbon units with 40.1042 and 34.0 point gaps.

annotations.error_summary: The agent misapplied the fallback for the no-downgrade case. The reference says that if no formal downgrade occurs, pressure cases should be identified by the quality-method penalty gap across the review cases; the agent continued to impose the customer-share and net-commission median filters used only for classifying method-driven downgrades.
annotations.evidence: The reference `quality_method_sensitivity` contains Blue Ribbon Japanese, Blue Ribbon American, The Meatball Shop American, and The Meatball Shop Italian, while the agent's filtered fallback returned only The Meatball Shop Italian.

annotations.error_summary: The agent used the wrong current positive set when identifying stress-only failures. A stress-only failure must have passed the current voucher-positive decision and then failed the combined stress check, but the agent filtered only on positive voucher-adjusted net commission and ignored the current pass label.
annotations.evidence: The reference has `stress_only_failures` as an empty list, while the agent reported Blue Ribbon Japanese and Blue Ribbon American because their voucher-adjusted net commission was positive even though they were already excluded by the current stricter-quality gate.

annotations.error_summary: The agent produced the reviewed units and attribution labels but omitted the required explanation of why each unit entered, stayed, weakened, or left the recommendation set. The task asks for the business reason, and the reference includes `main_business_reason` for each unit.
annotations.evidence: The reference gives reasons such as `left the set because stricter low-rating quality failed` and `entered and stayed positive through detailed economics and stress`, while the agent output only labels such as `stricter_quality_failure` and `stable_across_all_decision_views`.

annotations.error_summary: The final strategy used the correct core and exclusion units but again placed attribution labels in the `main_business_reason` field instead of the reason text assigned in the attribution view. This continues the missing-reason artifact from Task 31 and independently violates the current instruction to include only the main business reason.
annotations.evidence: The reference uses `entered and stayed positive through detailed economics and stress` for The Meatball Shop units and `left the set because stricter low-rating quality failed` for Blue Ribbon units, while the agent returned `stable_across_all_decision_views` and `stricter_quality_failure` as the reasons.

annotations.error_summary: The agent counted the physical CSV column-header line as a data row by reading the file with header=None. The task's question-text header is the first row after the CSV column names, so the correct raw count excludes the column-name line and the valid count removes only the question-text row.
annotations.evidence: The reference has raw_rows 23998 and valid_respondents 23997, while the agent reported 23999 and 23998 after treating the column-name line as part of the row count.

annotations.error_summary: The agent intended to count respondents shown each tool category by checking any sub-column, but its executed data handling treated opt-out selections labeled None as missing for the Business Intelligence and ML Serving blocks. That dropped opt-out-only respondents from the shown denominator, making shown equal at-least-1 for those two categories and producing 100 percent adoption rates.
annotations.evidence: The reference counts Business Intelligence shown as 5177 and ML Serving shown as 4641, while the agent reported 3127 and 1321, exactly matching its at-least-1 counts.

annotations.error_summary: The task required combining the active role-composition lift with the previously established global largest positive Q11 and Q16 experience skews. The agent failed to reuse those active skew-table artifacts and instead recalculated separate Q11 and Q16 anchors within each role, changing the meaning and scale of the role-intensity score.
annotations.evidence: The reference uses the same coding_anchor 4.2502 and ml_anchor 6.3519 for every role, but the agent used role-specific anchors such as 37.3342 and 20.5751 for Developer Advocate and ranked it first with score 7.1372.

annotations.error_summary: The rollback task required AutoML-only role composition and AutoML-only coding skew while keeping the current strict-view ML skew anchor unchanged. The agent carried forward the wrong role-specific anchor interpretation from task 13, recomputed role-specific AutoML coding anchors, and compared against the wrong strict top-5 role-intensity table.
annotations.evidence: The reference AutoML rollback top five are Data Architect, Developer Advocate, Machine Learning/ MLops Engineer, Data Scientist, and Data Engineer, while the agent included Statistician and Engineer (non-software) with inflated scores above 4.5.

annotations.error_summary: The active role-intensity table should have remained the strict cross-tool table from task 13 because task 14 was a rollback counterfactual. The agent treated the AutoML rollback hybrid view as the active role-intensity result and also retained the role-specific anchor mistake, so the role normalized concentration was computed from the wrong role-score table.
annotations.evidence: The industry normalized concentration matched at 1.1904, but the agent's role normalized concentration was 1.2846 instead of the reference 1.2993 because it used top role scores averaging 5.7096 rather than the strict-view top-five mean 2.7385.

annotations.error_summary: The task asked for the active strict role-intensity table, active asked-base industry table, and expanded small-organization boundary. The agent selected the wrong role-intensity state, using the inflated hybrid role-specific top-three role scores, while the industry front and expanded small-organization composite were otherwise correct.
annotations.evidence: The reference role_front is 2.9031 and resilience_score is 0.6192, while the agent used role_front 6.5098 and therefore reported resilience_score 1.3885.

annotations.error_summary: The current rollback calculation was locally consistent: it swapped in the narrow small-organization composite and kept the previous industry and role fronts unchanged. The answer was wrong because it inherited task 23's inflated role front and expanded resilience score.
annotations.evidence: The agent's percentage change matched the reference at -10.4626 percent, but both reported resilience scores were scaled from the wrong task-23 expanded score, giving 1.2432 and 1.3885 instead of 0.5544 and 0.6192.

annotations.error_summary: The broader-view rebuild required replacing only the composition-lift component and reusing the same strict cross-tool coding and ML skew anchors. The agent again recomputed role-specific strict anchors and compared against the already wrong strict top-five ranking from task 13.
annotations.evidence: The reference broader top five begin Data Architect, Machine Learning/ MLops Engineer, Data Scientist, Data Engineer, and Manager, while the agent reported Developer Advocate, Data Architect, Statistician, Engineer (non-software), and Data Administrator with scores above 4.4.

annotations.error_summary: The final-score formula, expanded small-organization multiplier, and top asked-base industry component were applied correctly. The top-five lists were wrong because the task inherited the incorrect narrow strict role-intensity table from task 13 and the incorrect broader role-intensity table from task 29.
annotations.evidence: The agent used the correct top industry asked-base adoption of 23.9316 percent but multiplied it by wrong role-intensity scores such as Developer Advocate 7.1372 and 6.9150, producing the wrong overlap set.

annotations.error_summary: The agent counted the physical CSV column-name row as a survey row by reading with header=None, so it included both the CSV header and the question-text row. The reference treats the CSV header as column names, counts rows including only the question-text header, then drops that row for valid respondents.
annotations.evidence: ground_code.py reads with the default header and reports 23998 raw rows and 23997 valid respondents, while code.py read with header=None and returned 23999 and 23998.

annotations.error_summary: The current counting logic was otherwise aligned with the shown and opt-out rules, but it inherited a cleaned_survey table created with pandas default NA parsing, which converted selected opt-out values equal to the literal string "None" into missing values. That made opt-out-only Business Intelligence and ML Serving respondents disappear from the shown denominator.
annotations.evidence: The reference preserves the opt-out label "None" and gets BI shown 5177 and ML Serving shown 4641, while the agent's inherited table made those shown counts equal the non-opt-out user counts 3127 and 1321.

annotations.error_summary: The agent computed the numeric shares correctly but did not use the established Q11 label order, instead reusing an alphabetically sorted label list from earlier work.
annotations.evidence: The reference order starts with "I have never written code", "< 1 years", and "1-3 years", whereas the agent output starts with "1-3 years", "10-20 years", and "20+ years".

annotations.error_summary: The agent misunderstood the coding and ML anchors as role-specific within-role skews and recomputed experience skews separately for each role. The reference takes the largest positive skew once from the active strict cross-tool coding and ML experience tables and adds those same two global anchors to every role's composition lift.
annotations.evidence: The reference uses coding_anchor 4.2502 and ml_anchor 6.3519 for every top role and ranks Data Architect first at 3.4375, while the agent gave Developer Advocate role-specific anchors 30.3279 and 20.0820 and score 6.3873.

annotations.error_summary: The rollback comparison mishandled the active states: it rolled back the adopter side but then recomputed AutoML coding anchors per role and retained per-role strict ML anchors inherited from the wrong Task 13 role-intensity table, instead of using the global AutoML coding anchor and unchanged global strict ML anchor. It also did not report the strict cross-tool top-5 list required for the comparison.
annotations.evidence: The reference v1 top 5 is Data Architect, Developer Advocate, Machine Learning/ MLops Engineer, Data Scientist, and Data Engineer and includes the current v2 top 5; the agent returned Developer Advocate, Statistician, Data Administrator, Data Architect, and Engineer (non-software) and only an overlap list.

annotations.error_summary: The industry side was correct, and the role-front averaging and normalization were locally the requested operations, but the role calculations used the already-wrong active role-intensity table from Task 13.
annotations.evidence: The agent matched the industry average and normalized concentration at 22.1491 and 1.1904, but its role average 5.2539 and role concentration 1.4354 came from the wrong Task 13 role scores rather than the reference 2.7385 and 1.2993.

annotations.error_summary: The formula and the industry and small-organization components were correct, but the role front used the corrupted active role-intensity top 3 from Task 13, inflating the role front and final resilience score.
annotations.evidence: Industry front 22.9146 and small-org composite 0.9308 match the reference, but the agent role_front 5.7917 and resilience 1.2354 differ from the reference 2.9031 and 0.6192.

annotations.error_summary: The narrow-boundary recomputation correctly reused the active industry front and changed only the small-organization composite, but those active fronts already contained the wrong role front and expanded resilience from Task 23, rooted in Task 13.
annotations.evidence: The percentage change -10.4626 matches because the same wrong role factor cancels, while both narrow and expanded scores are scaled too high at 1.1061 and 1.2354 instead of 0.5544 and 0.6192.

annotations.error_summary: The agent correctly formed the broader adopter group and rate, but it assigned the two count differences to the wrong prior-view comparison labels relative to the reference state mapping. The reference expects the broader view minus the strict managed-ML-plus-automated-ML view to be 982 and the broader view minus the AutoML-only view to be 760.

With the correct global anchors, the current computation would produce the reference v3 top 5.
annotations.evidence: The reference broader top 5 begins Data Architect at 2.8131, Machine Learning/ MLops Engineer at 2.7328, and Data Scientist at 2.6598, while the agent's inherited per-role anchors rank Developer Advocate, Statistician, and Data Administrator with scores above 5.

annotations.error_summary: The final score formula and common multiplier were locally reasonable, but both the narrower strict role-intensity table and the broader role-intensity table were already wrong, from Task 13 and the Task 29 rebuild. Thus both top-5 final lists and the overlap were wrong.
annotations.evidence: The reference strict and broad top lists are driven by Data Architect, Data Scientist, Machine Learning/ MLops Engineer, and Data Engineer, while the agent's lists reused the wrong Developer Advocate, Statistician, Data Administrator, Other, and Data Architect ordering.

This violated explicit instructions to count all joined rows while dropping missing engagement only for the engagement-index statistics, and it also confused the requested engagement-index/statistical population.

It omitted all product names, providers, and mean engagement values.

annotations.error_summary: The agent computed the dual-burden cutoffs over a restricted common engagement-feature universe instead of the intended full state-level crime table and full non-DC homelessness-rate table. That wrong median population selected AZ, MA, and MO rather than the reference six dual-burden states, so all phase gaps and the largest-gap phase were wrong.
annotations.evidence: Reference medians are crime 222.1418 and homelessness 29.767 with dual states AK, AZ, DE, NM, NV, SC; agent medians are 227.4765 and 16.6330 with dual states AZ, MA, MO.

annotations.error_summary: The agent selected the prior CM mean-weekly ranking from Task 8 as the top CM sub-function instead of recomputing the current task's explicitly requested overall mean-engagement ranking. That wrong prior artifact led it to choose Google Forms and compute its phases instead of Meet in the correct CM sub-function.
